newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to float more offshore bonds -TBA head.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to float more offshore bonds -TBA head.

text.p: The Thai government plans to float at least $500 million new Yankee and offshore bonds a year in the near future to sustain foreign interest in its economy, the Thai Bankers Association (TBA) president said on Wednesday.

Olarn Chaipravat, returning from a roadshow to the United States which resulted in the pricing of Thailand's $600 million Yankee bonds, said the government does not need any foreign financing for its annual budgets which have registered a surplus in each of the past nine years.
Despite this, Thai bond issues would help boost foreign understanding of the Thai economy and its strengths, he told reporters.
The finance ministry had told him that it would float more bonds every year even though the government enjoyed a fiscal surplus, he added.
The $600 million, 10-year Thai Yankee bonds launched last week in the United States, priced at 89 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, was the country's first in five years.
"We have missed the chance for full five years while other countries, including Korea, Malaysia and Singapore, have all done the same thing...," Olarn said.
He added that the $600 million issue was oversubscribed by about $400 million and about 30 percent of its investors were Asian.

Increased Thai government bonds would not erode the country's debt servicing position as the public sector's outstanding foreign debt amounted to only 19 percent of gross domestic product, a level he described as among the lowest in the world.
